title: Your First 24 Hours in Nanjing, Dealt as Cards
description: A measured first-day sequence from lake-edge bearings to dynastic monuments, modern history, a Yangtze dusk, Jiangsu cooking, and the lit streets of Qinhuai.

cards.title: Xuanwu Lake Park
cards.subtitle: Morning bearings beside water
cards.notes: Begin with the lake as your orientation point. A walk here places open water beside the city before the museum rooms and memorial architecture begin.
cards.short_summary: The municipal tourism bureau identifies Xuanwu Lake Park at No. 1 Xuanwu Alley and describes walking routes, lotus ponds, and boating within the park.
cards.source_title: Parks — Nanjing Municipal Bureau of Culture and Tourism

cards.title: Jiming Temple
cards.subtitle: A religious layer of the old capital
cards.notes: Let the second card introduce Nanjing’s Buddhist inheritance. The temple’s association with the Southern Dynasties gives the morning a longer historical register.
cards.short_summary: Nanjing’s municipal tourism bureau describes Jiming Temple as an old Buddhist temple and a center of Buddhism during the Southern Dynasties.
cards.source_title: Scenic Spots — Nanjing Municipal Bureau of Culture and Tourism

cards.title: Nanjing Museum
cards.subtitle: Six halls for the broader story
cards.notes: Use the late morning for objects rather than another skyline. Choose halls selectively: the institution spans history, art, special exhibitions, digital displays, Republican-era material, and intangible cultural heritage.
cards.short_summary: The city’s museum guide lists six components of Nanjing Museum: History, Art, Special Exhibition, Digital, Republic of China, and Intangible Cultural Heritage halls.
cards.source_title: Museums & Galleries — Nanjing Municipal Bureau of Culture and Tourism

cards.title: Presidential Palace of Nanjing
cards.subtitle: Modern government written into buildings
cards.notes: Shift from collections to a political site. Chinese gardens and Western office buildings share the grounds, making architectural contrast part of the modern-history lesson.
cards.short_summary: The municipal museum guide identifies the Presidential Palace as the Museum of Modern Chinese History and notes its gardens, Western office buildings, Sun Yat-sen plaque, and three exhibition areas.
cards.source_title: Museums & Galleries — Nanjing Municipal Bureau of Culture and Tourism

cards.entity_name: The Memorial Hall of the Victims in Nanjing Massacre by Japanese Invaders
cards.title: The Memorial Hall of the Victims in Nanjing Massacre by Japanese Invaders
cards.subtitle: A deliberate pause for historical memory
cards.notes: Give this stop unhurried attention and keep its role distinct from general sightseeing. The memorial stands where victims’ remains were found and frames its work around remembrance and peace.
cards.short_summary: The institution states that the memorial was built on the original site where victims’ remains were found and opened in 1985.
cards.source_title: Museum — The Memorial Hall of the Victims in Nanjing Massacre by Japanese Invaders

cards.title: Zhongshan Pier
cards.subtitle: Dusk at the Yangtze
cards.notes: After the memorial, move outdoors and let the river reset the scale of the day. The pier offers a sunset view with the Nanjing Yangtze River Bridge in the distance.
cards.short_summary: A Nanjing municipal profile specifically describes viewing sunset from Zhongshan Pier with the Yangtze River Bridge visible beyond it.
cards.source_title: A Nepalese Professor in Nanjing — NanjingEnglish

cards.title: Jiangnan Wok
cards.subtitle: Dinner through a Jiangsu kitchen
cards.notes: Make dinner the food card rather than squeezing snacks between monuments. The restaurant’s own menu names Jinling classic salted duck alongside river shrimp, seasonal vegetables, tofu with crab meat, and other regional preparations.
cards.short_summary: Jiangnan Wok’s direct menu documents Jinling salted duck and a range of Jiangsu-style river, vegetable, tofu, and rice-cake dishes.
cards.source_title: Jiangnan Wok Food Menu — Shangri-La Nanjing

cards.entity_name: Nanjing Mendong Historical and Cultural Block
cards.title: Nanjing Mendong Historical and Cultural Block
cards.subtitle: An evening street interlude
cards.notes: Walk the block as a change of rhythm after dinner: shopfronts and pedestrian space replace display cases. Its official designation as a historical-cultural and demonstration pedestrian block gives this card a clear urban role.
cards.short_summary: The Nanjing Municipal Commerce Bureau lists the Mendong Historical and Cultural Block at No. 63-2 Jianzi Lane and identifies it as a Jiangsu demonstration pedestrian street.
cards.source_title: Characteristic Commercial Blocks — Nanjing Municipal Commerce Bureau

cards.title: Nanjing Confucius Temple
cards.subtitle: Close the evening beside the Qinhuai
cards.notes: End the first evening where temple precinct, river, streets, gardens, and pavilions meet. Treat it as a living district rather than a single façade.
cards.short_summary: The city tourism bureau describes the Confucius Temple scenic area as an integration of ancient sites, gardens, painted boats, streets, pavilions, and local customs beside the Qinhuai River.
cards.source_title: Scenic Spots — Nanjing Municipal Bureau of Culture and Tourism

cards.title: Ming Xiaoling Mausoleum
cards.subtitle: Next morning on the spirit path
cards.notes: Use the final card for a quieter return to the dynastic city. The winding spirit path and main tomb complex connect Nanjing to the first Ming emperor and to a wider lineage of imperial-tomb design.
cards.short_summary: UNESCO identifies Xiaoling as the tomb of the first Ming emperor and explains that its design established a model followed by later imperial tombs.
cards.source_title: Imperial Tombs of the Ming and Qing Dynasties — UNESCO World Heritage Centre
